description: The National Geochemical Database project assembles, reformats, corrects and archives historical results from the geochemical analysis of millions of geologic samples collected in USGS studies, to give an accurate, accessible multi-element database of the nation's surficial materials. Its data releases include geochemical data for selected areas, such as the Idaho Primitive Area (version 1.2, June 2022), analyses of more than 1,700 archived stream-sediment samples from Alaska (September 2021) and the National Geochemical Database on Ore Deposits legacy data on nearly 30,000 historic ore and ore-related rock samples. It is run by the USGS Geology, Geophysics, and Geochemistry Science Center with the Mineral Resources Program and the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative. Coverage is the United States. The data are provided to USGS researchers, other federal agencies, state geological surveys and environmental protection agencies, and releases are available free through USGS data releases. Caveats: legacy data come from many decades of methods and detection limits, so values need care when compared. For simulation it gives baseline element concentrations for mineral resource, contamination and critical mineral supply studies. It is related to the USGS global critical minerals mines, deposits and districts record in this catalogue.
